tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Excise duty of Rs. 21.65 Cr alongwith applicable interest and penalty was demanded on Industrial Promotion Subsidy (IPS) received during August-2011 to April 2015. Commissioner, CGST, Kolhapur passed the Order in Original in favor of KOEL in Mar-2019 dropping the entire demand. In February 2022, Commissioner, CGST, Kolhapur Commissionerate filed an appeal before Hon'ble CESTAT, Mumbai against the order in original.
tax_litigation.status: The appeal is pending before Hon'ble Customs, Excise And Service Tax Appellate Tribunal (CESTAT), Mumbai bench. There is no further development for Q3 of FY 2025-26.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Tran-1 credit of Rs.18.93 Cr disallowed and imposed equal penalty and interest as applicable
tax_litigation.status: An appeal has been filed by the Company against the order before the Commissioner- Appeal, CGST, Pune-II and the same is pending. There is no further development for Q3 of FY 2025-26.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: Excise duty exemption denied on pump set and differential duty of Rs. 11.70 Cr demanded imposing a penalty of Rs. 4 Cr and interest as applicable
tax_litigation.status: An appeal has been filed by the Company against the order before Hon'ble Customs, Excise And Service Tax Appellate Tribunal (CESTAT), Ahmedabad and the same is pending. There is no further development for Q3 of FY 2025-26.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The ITD has made additions to the returned income of the Company for FY 2014-15 on account of capital subsidy received from Government of Maharashtra, disallowance of provision for warranty and few other expenses/ deductions during the scrutiny assessment order passed u/s 143(3) of the Income Tax Act, 1961. Quantum of claim is Rs. 26,84,25,463.
tax_litigation.status: The company has filed an appeal before the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals) (CIT(A)/ First Appellate Authority) and the same is currently pending. Based on the past precedents in Company's own case as well as other judicial pronouncements, the Company is of the view that the likelihood of these additions being deleted by the appellate authorities is high and there may not be any material claim against the Company which may have any impact on the company. There is no further development for Q3 of FY 2025-26.

tax_litigation.status: The company has filed an appeal before the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals) (CIT(A)/ First Appellate Authority) and the same is currently pending.Based on the past precedents in Company's own case as well as other judicial pronouncements, the Company is of the view that the likelihood of these additions being deleted by the appellate authorities is high and there may not be any material claim against the Company which may have any impact on the company. There is no further development for Q3 of FY 2025-26.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The ITD had made additions to the returned income of the Company for FY 2022-23 on account of disallowance of provision for warranty during the scrutiny assessment order passed u/s 143(3) of the Income Tax Act, 1961. During the course of the scrutiny assessment the SCN was issued on 27th February 2025, proposing total disallowances having a tax impact of INR 19.17 Cr. However, post filing the submission clarifying the factual position on the proposed disallowances as mentioned in the SCN the ITD passed the final order dated 24th March 2025, making the disallowance only in respect of provision for warranty having a Tax impact of 12.93 Cr.Being aggrieved, KOEL has filed an appeal before the Comissioner of Income Tax (Appeals) on April 11, 2025.
tax_litigation.status: The company has filed an appeal before the Commissioner of Income Tax (Appeals) (CIT(A)/ First Appellate Authority) and the same is currently pending. Based on the past precedents in Company's own case as well as other judicial pronouncements, the Company is of the view that the likelihood of these additions being deleted by the courts of law is very high and there will not be any material claim against the Company which will have any impact on the Company. There is no further development for Q3 of FY 2025-26.

guidance.statement: Remains committed to becoming a USD 2 billion company by FY30
Aspiration to be a $2 billion revenue enterprise by FY30, close to INR16,600 crores
Endeavour to earn a higher double-digit EBITDA margin by FY30

industry: Industrials > Capital Goods > Industrial Products > Compressors, Pumps & Diesel Engines

operating_notes.text: KOEL sold upwards of 50,000 DG units in FY26, up 41%, against an 18% market growth to about 179,000 units including telecom.
Working capital at FY26 end: payables about 60 days, receivables about 41 days, inventory about 48 days (from 66 days in Q3FY26).
Arka AUM grew 10% to ₹7,947 Cr with NIM income up 11% to ₹266 Cr; GNPA 1.2% and NNPA 0.3% at 31 March 2026.
Standalone segment revenue in Q1FY27: power gen ₹720 Cr (+18%), industrial ₹368 Cr (+19%), distribution and aftermarket ₹268 Cr (+20%), international ₹106 Cr (-11%).
KOEL Fluid Dynamics revenue was broadly flat at ₹294 Cr with domestic sales up and exports down; Arka AUM stood at ₹7,651 Cr across about 136 branches.
Cash conversion cycle was 25 days with inventory days up slightly to 264.
